findings.highlight: some relation to that old man
findings.evidenceJa: 少なからず縁がある
findings.governingReading: Kirei says he has no small degree of connection with Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English reduces an emphatically substantial connection to an unspecified relation.

findings.evidenceJa: 申し合わせたように教会を後にした
findings.governingReading: Without looking at each other’s expressions, they leave as if by prior arrangement.
findings.explanation: The English preserves joint departure but removes their unspoken coordination.

findings.evidenceJa: 互いの表情も見ないまま
findings.governingReading: They depart without seeing each other’s expressions.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes this to not looking at each other, losing the guarded inability to read expression.

findings.evidenceJa: ハイヤーを飛ばして森に着く頃
findings.governingReading: They speed to the forest in a hired car as dawn begins.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the hired-car category and the urgent speed of travel.

findings.evidenceJa: 黒塗りの外車
findings.governingReading: Kirei stops a black-painted foreign car on the public road.
findings.explanation: The English removes the vehicle’s conspicuous color and foreign make.

findings.highlight: how are you going to help me
findings.evidenceJa: 協力するって、何を協力するんだよ
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks what their cooperation will consist of.
findings.explanation: The English makes Kirei’s help unilateral and assigns Shirou as its beneficiary, weakening the bounded alliance.

findings.evidenceJa: 得体の知れない学生
findings.governingReading: A taxi driver would see Shirou as an unidentified or inexplicable student asking for a remote ride after three.
findings.explanation: The English judges Shirou suspicious rather than merely unknown and strange to the driver.

findings.highlight: Kotomine gives orders to the driver
findings.evidenceJa: 淡々と運転手に指示を出す
findings.governingReading: Kirei gives the grim contingency instructions matter-of-factly.
findings.explanation: The English removes his emotionally flat delivery.

findings.evidenceJa: 棒のような物
findings.governingReading: Kirei tosses Shirou an object that initially looks like a stick.
findings.explanation: The English prematurely supplies length and thinness before Shirou identifies the weapon.

findings.evidenceJa: 西洋の細剣に近い
findings.governingReading: Among weapons Shirou knows, it is closest to a Western slender thrusting sword.
findings.explanation: The English names the comparison specifically as a rapier, making an approximate lay description sound classificatory.

findings.highlight: Assassin’s dirk made into a sword
findings.evidenceJa: 短剣を長剣にしたような剣
findings.governingReading: It resembles Assassin’s dagger lengthened into a long sword.
findings.explanation: The English removes the long-sword endpoint and leaves a dagger made into an unspecified sword.

findings.evidenceJa: 幽霊どもに鉛弾は効かん
findings.governingReading: Kirei specifically says lead bullets do not work on the ghosts.
findings.explanation: The English universalizes the ineffectiveness to all bullets.

findings.highlight: you’re not trained to use them
findings.evidenceJa: おまえには扱い辛いものだ
findings.governingReading: Submachine guns would be difficult for Shirou to handle.
findings.explanation: The English infers a lack of training as the reason, converting practical unsuitability into biography.

findings.evidenceJa: 一キロ弱程
findings.governingReading: The Black Key weighs a little less than one kilogram.
findings.explanation: The English loses the below-one-kilogram bound.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔術ではなく秘跡
findings.governingReading: The Black Key is a sacrament rather than magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English uses the unstable broad term “magic,” blurring the technical distinction Kirei explicitly makes.

findings.evidenceJa: 我々の専売特許
findings.governingReading: Dealing with spiritual bodies is the Church’s special province or stock-in-trade.
findings.explanation: The English makes it an exclusive legal or moral right rather than specialized expertise.

findings.highlight: If you use your magic on that sword
findings.evidenceJa: 刀身におまえの魔術を載せれば
findings.governingReading: Shirou can load or overlay his magecraft onto the blade.
findings.explanation: The English removes the blade as exact locus and the layering mechanism.

findings.highlight: we’ll think about that after we get there
findings.evidenceJa: その時はその時だ
findings.governingReading: If the castle is already empty, Kirei accepts that they will deal with that situation when it arises.
findings.explanation: The English turns pragmatic acceptance into postponing thought until arrival.

findings.highlight: find out where Matou Sakura went
findings.evidenceJa: 手掛かり程度は見つけだせる
findings.governingReading: At minimum they may find a clue to where Sakura went.
findings.explanation: The English promotes finding limited evidence into determining her destination.

findings.evidenceJa: 短く深呼吸をする
findings.governingReading: Shirou takes one short deep breath before following Kirei.
findings.explanation: The English removes its brief, controlled duration.

findings.evidenceJa: あっちにはセイバーまでいる
findings.governingReading: On the opposing side, even Saber is present.
findings.explanation: The English invents a plural group possessing Saber, though Shirou is distinguishing the shadow and Sakura uncertainly.

findings.highlight: What can I do to Sakura?
findings.evidenceJa: ああなってしまった桜相手にどうすればいい
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks what he can do when facing Sakura after she has become like that.
findings.explanation: The English drops her transformed condition and can sound like deliberation over an action against Sakura.

findings.highlight: take Sakura back to my house
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮の家まで連れ帰る
findings.governingReading: Shirou wants to bring Sakura back to the Emiya home.
findings.explanation: The English turns the named household she joined into generic personal property.

findings.highlight: You should know that better than me
findings.evidenceJa: おまえの方が判っているのではないか
findings.governingReading: Kirei asks whether Shirou himself already understands that immediate confrontation is hopeless.
findings.explanation: The English adds a comparison claiming Shirou knows it better than Kirei.

findings.evidenceJa: 今回は諦めろ
findings.governingReading: Kirei tells Shirou to give up the Sakura confrontation on this occasion.
findings.explanation: “Let it go” is vague enough to suggest abandoning Sakura or the goal, rather than postponing this attempt.

findings.highlight: if we can put Illyasviel under your care
findings.evidenceJa: イリヤスフィールをこちらで保護すれば
findings.governingReading: If their side secures Illya’s protection, they will gain time.
findings.explanation: The English assigns Illya specifically to Shirou’s care and changes protective custody into placement.

findings.evidenceJa: まだ猶予は出来る
findings.governingReading: Rescuing Illya creates additional time or respite before the crisis closes.
findings.explanation: The English turns time gained into an unspecified chance, obscuring what rescue changes.

findings.evidenceJa: イリヤは殺させない
findings.governingReading: Shirou will not allow anyone, specifically Sakura, to kill Illya.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the commitment to preventing Illya’s death by any cause and weakens the actor relation paired with the next clause.

findings.evidenceJa: 二時間強
findings.governingReading: They have spent more than two hours in the forest.
findings.explanation: The English removes the excess beyond two hours.

findings.highlight: if we are to fight Matou Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: 万が一、間桐桜と戦う事になれば
findings.governingReading: In the unlikely event they are forced to fight Sakura, Kirei will retreat.
findings.explanation: The English removes the contingency’s low probability and makes the fight sound expected.

findings.evidenceJa: 黒化した間桐桜
findings.governingReading: Kirei describes Matou Sakura after undergoing blackening or corruption.
findings.explanation: The English turns a state or process into the categorical proper-name-like label “Black Sakura.”

findings.evidenceJa: 黒化ってなんだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou challenges Kirei’s term for Sakura’s process of blackening or corruption.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the process to the color adjective “Black.”

findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜の精神を繋ぎとめる
findings.governingReading: Shirou can only keep Sakura’s psyche tethered or prevent it from slipping away until the shadow is born.
findings.explanation: The English turns maintenance of continuity into generic protection, losing the mechanism and stakes.

findings.highlight: I don’t know how to protect her mind
findings.evidenceJa: その繋ぎ止める方法がわからない
findings.governingReading: Shirou does not know how to perform the tethering Kirei just described.
findings.explanation: The repeated English wording erases the continuity mechanism and makes the problem general protection.

findings.evidenceJa: 刻一刻と影そのものになろうとしている
findings.governingReading: Shirou fears Sakura is becoming the shadow itself with every passing moment.
findings.explanation: The English retains gradual change but removes the urgent moment-by-moment progression.

findings.evidenceJa: 多少の共感はある
findings.governingReading: Kirei allows that some resonance, correspondence, or shared sensation may exist between Sakura and the shadow.
findings.explanation: The English uses emotional sympathy, misleadingly suggesting compassion or agreement.

findings.evidenceJa: 胎内にいるモノを摘出
findings.governingReading: If the entity were literally in Sakura’s womb, removing what is inside the womb would solve the problem.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the location to her body and weakens Kirei’s rejection of Shirou’s literal pregnancy reading.

findings.evidenceJa: 栄養
findings.governingReading: Sakura supplies the entity with nourishment as its vessel.
findings.explanation: The English replaces biological nourishment with abstract energy, weakening the birth metaphor.

findings.evidenceJa: 実像
findings.governingReading: Sakura supplies the formless entity with a real image or material presence.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the technical contrast between formless main body and real image to generic form.

findings.evidenceJa: 依り代
findings.governingReading: Sakura is the vessel or material anchor through which the entity receives nourishment and presence.
findings.explanation: The English calls her a host, importing a parasitic-organism relation and losing ritual anchoring.

findings.highlight: the magic circle and the brain
findings.evidenceJa: 大頭脳たる魔法陣
findings.governingReading: The foundational Grail is a magic circle functioning as the great brain that governs the ritual’s rules.
findings.explanation: The English coordinates the magic circle and brain as two separate things instead of an appositional identity.

findings.highlight: they summon the Holy Grail into the Holy Grail the people prepared
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯を、人間が用意した聖杯に降霊させる
findings.governingReading: Humans prepare a receiving Grail into which the land’s Grail is called down as a spirit.
findings.explanation: The English repeats “Holy Grail” without relational clarification and omits the spirit-descent mechanism, making the distinction nearly unintelligible.

findings.evidenceJa: 人の手による原因
findings.governingReading: If the war is artificially caused, Shirou reasons that a corresponding human-made cause or mechanism must exist.
findings.explanation: The English uses awkward repetition and leaves the causal mechanism abstract.

findings.evidenceJa: 大掛かりな起動式
findings.governingReading: Shirou considers finding and destroying the large-scale activation formula or system.
findings.explanation: The English equates the operating formula with the magic circle itself, narrowing mechanism to object.

findings.evidenceJa: 桜を犯している影
findings.governingReading: The shadow is violating, corrupting, or afflicting Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English adds her body as the exclusive locus, though the surrounding threat includes psyche and identity.

findings.highlight: The Tohsaka family are the supervisors of this land
findings.evidenceJa: この土地の管理者は遠坂だ
findings.governingReading: Tohsaka is the administrator or manager of this land.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the office into the family and uses supervisory language that weakens formal territorial authority.

findings.evidenceJa: 凛ならば教えられている筈
findings.governingReading: As successor, Rin should have been taught the entrance’s location.
findings.explanation: The English removes instruction and turns inherited transmission into unexplained knowledge.

findings.highlight: she and Matou Sakura will be disposed of as the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜もイリヤスフィールも聖杯として使い捨てられる
findings.governingReading: Both Sakura and Illya will be used up and discarded as Grails.
findings.explanation: The English uses singular “the Holy Grail,” obscuring their separate vessel roles.

findings.highlight: the completion of the magic circle
findings.evidenceJa: 起動式の成就
findings.governingReading: Kirei’s goal is fulfillment or successful operation of the activation formula.
findings.explanation: The English makes his goal constructional completion of the circle rather than completion of what it activates.

findings.highlight: what comes from Matou Sakurano, what is trying to become her
findings.evidenceJa: 間桐桜から変化するモノいや、間桐桜になろうとしているモノ
findings.governingReading: Kirei corrects “the thing changing from Sakura” to “the thing trying to become Sakura.”
findings.explanation: The English fuses “Sakura” and “no” into malformed text and weakens the audible self-correction.

findings.highlight: Unlike Zouken, I have no wish
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯のような望みはない
findings.governingReading: Kirei says he has no desire like Zouken’s concerning the emerging thing.
findings.explanation: Although the English retains “Unlike Zouken,” its absolute “no wish” can deny Kirei all desire rather than the compared acquisitive wish.

findings.highlight: I will die just like everybody else
findings.evidenceJa: 私とて例外なく死に絶える
findings.governingReading: Kirei says even he will die out without exception if Sakura becomes the phenomenon called hell.
findings.explanation: The English adds everybody else’s death as an explicit comparison.

findings.highlight: it must be the desire to be born
findings.evidenceJa: 生まれたいという一念だけではないのか
findings.governingReading: Kirei rhetorically proposes that the only pure wish may be the single-minded desire to be born.
findings.explanation: The English promotes his question into certainty and removes the single-minded exclusivity of 一念.

findings.evidenceJa: 幸福を得られる
findings.governingReading: Kirei says humans can obtain happiness merely by existing.
findings.explanation: “Earn” introduces merit or labor into an argument that explicitly grounds happiness in bare existence.

findings.evidenceJa: 何が正しいのか”を受け入れる機能
findings.governingReading: Humans possess a function for accepting what is right after learning enjoyment from zero.
findings.explanation: The English changes acceptance into learning and removes the claimed human faculty.

findings.highlight: The person’s knowledge will decide that
findings.evidenceJa: 人間の学習次第
findings.governingReading: Whether a person becomes good or evil depends on human learning.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes the stock of knowledge for the developmental process central to Kirei’s argument.

findings.evidenceJa: 自らを育てた『自己』
findings.governingReading: Responsibility lies partly with the self that cultivated or raised itself.
findings.explanation: The English changes reflexive self-formation into a separate “self” that raised the addressee, breaking the philosophical relation.

findings.highlight: There is no crime in receiving birth
findings.evidenceJa: 生まれ出る事には何の罪もない
findings.governingReading: The entity bears no guilt simply for emerging into birth.
findings.explanation: “Receiving birth” is non-English and weakens the entity’s own emergence.

findings.highlight: the evil that will be born
findings.evidenceJa: 生まれようとしている“魔”
findings.governingReading: Kirei intends to bless the demonic or supernatural evil-being trying to be born from Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English turns the entity into abstract moral evil and makes birth certain rather than attempted.

findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯から桜を解放させようとしている
findings.governingReading: Kirei is genuinely trying to free Sakura from Zouken.
findings.explanation: The English adds control as the exclusive relation, omitting physical possession, exploitation, and ritual use.

findings.evidenceJa: 共存できない生き物
findings.governingReading: Shirou and Kirei are living beings whose natures cannot coexist.
findings.explanation: The English turns the people into abstract “lives,” weakening irreconcilable creaturely nature.

findings.highlight: an ally that’s better than anyone
findings.evidenceJa: この場において何よりも勝る味方
findings.governingReading: In this situation Shirou has gained an ally whose value surpasses anything else available.
findings.explanation: The English turns situational operational value into comparison against people, with “better” left undefined.
